s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower back pain with radiating symptoms and evidence of a spinal lesion with potential metastatic disease
salient_findings: Lower back pain radiating to both groins for 2 months
Mixed sclerotic and lytic lesion in the T12 vertebral body
Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules and mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy
key_facts: 44-year-old man with no significant past medical history
Lower back pain radiating to both groins for 2 months
Normal vital signs
Unremarkable physical examination
Normal routine laboratory studies
Mixed sclerotic and lytic lesion in the T12 vertebral body on CT scan
Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules on CT scan
Mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy on CT scan
CT-guided biopsy of a pulmonary nodule demonstrated a malignant neoplasm
Tumor cells composed of spindle cells
Immunohistochemical staining positive for Bcl-2, vimentin, EMA, CD56, CD99, and TLE-1
Immunohistochemical staining negative for CD34, CD10, p63, cytokeratin, S100, desmin, and synaptophysin

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Positive CD99 staining and presence of spinal lesion with radiating symptoms

shortlist.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Spindle cell morphology and positive staining for CD56 and Bcl-2

shortlist.label: Hemangiopericytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Spindle cell morphology and positive staining for CD56 and vimentin

shortlist.label: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Spindle cell morphology and presence of spinal lesion

shortlist.label: Primitive neuroectodermal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of spinal lesion and radiating symptoms with malignant neoplasm composed of spindle cells

raw.rationale: The presence of a mixed sclerotic and lytic lesion in the T12 vertebral body, multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules, and mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy, along with the immunohistochemical staining profile (positive for CD99) is highly suggestive of Ewing's sarcoma.

rejected.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
rejected.why: Typically has a more benign appearance on imaging and lacks the aggressive features seen in this case

rejected.label: Hemangiopericytoma
rejected.why: Usually has a distinct vascular pattern on imaging and lacks the specific immunohistochemical staining profile seen in this case

rejected.label: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor
rejected.why: Typically has a different immunohistochemical staining profile and is often associated with neurofibromatosis type 1

rejected.label: Primitive neuroectodermal tumor
rejected.why: While similar to Ewing's sarcoma, the lack of specific mention of neuroectodermal markers makes Ewing's sarcoma a more likely diagnosis
